note: Where each land animal lives and how often a walker meets it. Read by gen/fauna.cpp (the cook places residents) and native/world.cpp (they live their lives). Ranges are countries (ISO 3166-1, assets/world/countries.geojson) narrowed by boxes [west, south, east, north] where a species holds only part of a country. Densities are individuals per km2 of optimal habitat, orders of magnitude from published counts; detectability is the share of them a walker can meet at the species' peak hour (the rest are hidden, underground or far in cover). Months are the northern temperate calendar (flipped south of the equator, ignored in the tropics). Fish, marine animals, birds and bats are not placed yet (PLAN: Animals update). behaviour.home is the radius of a home range, metres: a group is at one point of it at a time.

settlement.note: How a species answers the built share b around a point (buildings and urban ground within 64 m): wild animals leave as b grows, commensals need it.

species.name: Renard roux
species.basis: IUCN range (Holarctic; introduced in Australia). Rural densities 1-3 per km2, more in some cities.

species.name: Renard polaire
species.basis: IUCN range: Arctic tundra and Iceland. 0.1-1 per km2.

species.name: Loup gris
species.basis: IUCN and national monitoring ranges; packs at 1-4 wolves per 100 km2.

species.name: Loup arctique
species.basis: High Arctic of Canada and Greenland; very low densities.

species.name: Ours brun
species.basis: IUCN range; 1-20 per 100 km2 (Carpathians densest in Europe). Hibernates in winter.

species.name: Ours noir
species.basis: IUCN range: forests of Canada, the United States and northern Mexico; 10-100 per 100 km2.

species.name: Ours polaire
species.basis: IUCN range: Arctic sea ice and coasts; under one bear per 100 km2.

species.name: Sanglier
species.basis: IUCN range plus feral populations (United States, Australia, South America). 2-10 per km2 in European forests.

species.name: Cerf élaphe
species.basis: IUCN range plus introductions (New Zealand, Argentina, Chile, Australia). 1-5 per km2 in European forests; herds of hinds, stags apart.

species.name: Wapiti
species.basis: Rocky Mountains and western ranges of North America, eastern reintroductions small.

species.name: Chevreuil
species.basis: IUCN range (Europe to Turkey and the Caspian; Siberian roe deer further east). 5-20 per km2 in French woodland and farmland.
species.assetNote: No roe deer model of its own: the CC0 hind (doe, 4 800 triangles, its own clips) at roe deer size. The 0 A.D. deer was dropped: its clips come from another skeleton and fold its legs.

species.name: Daim
species.basis: Native to Anatolia, introduced across Europe and elsewhere, often in parks and estates.
species.assetNote: The CC0 hind at fallow deer size, without the spotted coat: the spotted 0 A.D. deer moves its legs wrong.

species.name: Cerf axis
species.basis: Indian subcontinent; 10-60 per km2 in reserves, far fewer outside.
species.assetNote: The CC0 hind at chital size, without the spots.

species.name: Cerf de Virginie
species.basis: IUCN range: southern Canada to northern South America; 5-20 per km2, common in suburbs.
species.assetNote: The CC0 hind at white-tailed deer size.

species.name: Lapin de garenne
species.basis: Native to Iberia, introduced across Europe, Australia, New Zealand and Chile. Highly variable, 1-50 per km2.

species.name: Lapin à queue blanche
species.basis: IUCN range: southern Canada to north-western South America.

species.name: Lion
species.basis: IUCN range: savannas of eastern and southern Africa, remnant West African populations, Gir forest in India. 1-20 per 100 km2.

species.name: Éléphant de savane
species.basis: IUCN range: savannas of eastern and southern Africa and Sahel remnants; 0.1-3 per km2 (Chobe densest).

species.name: Éléphant de forêt
species.basis: IUCN range: Central African rainforests and West African forest remnants.

species.name: Éléphant d'Asie
species.basis: IUCN range: India, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and South-East Asia.

species.name: Girafe
species.basis: IUCN range: savannas and open woodland of eastern and southern Africa, Niger's West African giraffes.

species.name: Zèbre des plaines
species.basis: IUCN range: grasslands of eastern and southern Africa.

species.name: Gnou bleu
species.basis: IUCN range: eastern and southern African grasslands.

species.name: Gazelle de Thomson
species.basis: Short-grass plains of Kenya and Tanzania.
species.assetNote: The gazelle carries the 0 A.D. deer clips, made on another skeleton: its standing clips are retargeted, its walk and run fold its legs and are not played, so it grazes where it stands.

species.name: Gazelle dorcas
species.basis: Sahara, Sahel and the Red Sea hills; sparse.
species.assetNote: The gazelle carries the 0 A.D. deer clips, made on another skeleton: its standing clips are retargeted, its walk and run fold its legs and are not played, so it grazes where it stands.

species.name: Hippopotame
species.basis: IUCN range: rivers and lakes of sub-Saharan Africa. In the water by day, grazing ashore at night.

species.name: Crocodile du Nil
species.basis: IUCN range: sub-Saharan Africa, the upper Nile and Madagascar. Basks on banks by day.

species.name: Crocodile marin
species.basis: Estuaries and coasts from India to northern Australia.

species.name: Crocodile des marais
species.basis: Freshwater of the Indian subcontinent and south-east Iran.

species.name: Crocodile américain
species.basis: Coasts and rivers from southern Florida and Mexico to Peru and the Caribbean.

species.name: Rhinocéros blanc
species.basis: Southern Africa (Kruger and Hluhluwe-iMfolozi hold most), reintroductions in Kenya, Uganda and Zimbabwe.

species.name: Tigre
species.basis: IUCN range: India and fragments from the Sundarbans to the Russian Far East and Sumatra; 1-15 per 100 km2.

species.name: Gorille de l'Ouest
species.basis: IUCN range: rainforests of Gabon, Congo, south Cameroon, Equatorial Guinea, the Central African Republic and Cabinda.

species.name: Gorille de l'Est
species.basis: Eastern DR Congo, the Virunga volcanoes and Bwindi.

species.name: Dromadaire
species.basis: Herded across the Sahara, the Sahel, the Horn of Africa, Arabia, south Iran, Pakistan and Rajasthan; feral in central Australia.

species.name: Vache
species.basis: Grazed on pasture in Europe, the Americas, Oceania, temperate Asia and southern Africa; often housed in northern winters.

species.name: Zébu
species.basis: The humped cattle of South and South-East Asia, the Sahel, the Horn of Africa, Madagascar and tropical Latin America. Free-roaming in Indian and Nepali streets.

species.name: Bovin sanga
species.basis: The cattle of East and Southern Africa (Ankole, Nguni, Afrikaner).

species.name: Mouton
species.basis: Flocks on rough grazing: the British Isles, Iceland, New Zealand, Australia, the Mediterranean, the Middle East, Central Asia, the Andes and Patagonia.

species.name: Chèvre
species.basis: Herded in Mediterranean hills, Africa, the Middle East, South Asia, China and Latin America.

species.name: Cheval
species.basis: Pastured across Europe, the Americas and Oceania; semi-free on the steppes of Mongolia and Kazakhstan. Breeds follow their country.

species.name: Âne
species.basis: Working donkeys of Africa, the Middle East, South Asia and Latin America; a few in Mediterranean Europe.
species.assetNote: The 0 A.D. donkey walk barely moves its legs: it would glide, so the donkey stands.

species.name: Cochon
species.basis: Pigs kept outdoors: the Iberian dehesa, village pigs of the Pacific, South-East Asia, southern China, non-Muslim Africa and Latin America. Most European pigs never go out.

species.name: Chat domestique
species.basis: Owned and street cats wherever people live; most are indoors or out of sight at any moment. Street cats abound around the Mediterranean and in Turkey.
species.assetNote: The cats' rigs only carry deformation-check clips: they sit still and look about, never walk.

species.name: Rat surmulot
species.basis: Every city, mostly out of sight underground and in buildings; met at night by bins, quays and parks.
species.assetNote: The rat's rig only carries deformation-check clips: it sniffs about and darts off unanimated.

species.name: Souris grise
species.basis: In houses and barns worldwide, more often in the country, at night.
species.assetNote: The mouse's only clip is a short in-place motion: it stays put and darts off unanimated.

species.name: Lézard des murailles
species.basis: Southern and central Europe on walls, rocks, vineyards and railway banks; out in sunshine from March to October.
species.assetNote: The lizard's rig only carries deformation-check clips: it basks and bobs its head, and darts off unanimated.

species.name: Dendrobate azureus
species.basis: Forest islands of southern Suriname and the bordering Brazilian Sipaliwini savanna.
species.assetNote: Deformation-check clips only: the frog sits still.

species.name: Ranitomeya amazonica
species.basis: Lowland Amazon rainforest around Iquitos and the bordering basins.
species.assetNote: Deformation-check clips only: the frog sits still.

species.name: Rainette aux yeux rouges
species.basis: Lowland rainforest from southern Mexico to north-western Colombia; out at night near ponds.
species.assetNote: Deformation-check clips only: the frog sits still.

species.name: Tortue de Reeves
species.basis: Ponds, rice fields and slow rivers of eastern China, Korea, Japan and Taiwan; basks by day in the warm months.
species.assetNote: Deformation-check clips only: the turtle basks without moving.

species.name: Monarque
species.basis: The Americas, eastern Australia, New Zealand and southern Iberia; overwinters by the million in the oyamel forests of Michoacán.

species.name: Guêpe commune
species.basis: Holarctic, introduced in Australia, New Zealand and South America; workers fly from July to September.

species.name: Araignée (maison)
species.basis: Some spider lives in nearly every house; one big enough to notice, on a wall or in a ceiling corner, is met in a few houses in a hundred, more in autumn when males wander.
species.standIn: spider_garden is a wasp spider (Argiope bruennichi), a meadow species: it stands in for the house spiders until a house spider model of the same grade exists.

species.name: Fourmi noire des jardins
species.basis: Holarctic; a foraging trail into a kitchen in the warm months.
